problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable, globally L-smooth convex function f:E→ℝ, with an attained minimum.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/InexactGradientStronglyConvex.lean: spec.admissible, gradient existence, upper quadratic inequality, lower quadratic inequality, and minimizer existence.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: Global μ-strong convexity: f(y)≥f(x)+⟪∇f(x),y−x⟫+(μ/2)‖y−x‖², with 0<μ≤L. A minimizer xstar satisfies ‖x0−xstar‖≤R.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: A query x∈E returns g∈E satisfying ‖g−∇f(x)‖≤α‖∇f(x)‖+δ for every call index and seed. Only gradient vectors are returned; function values are unavailable. The budget counts individual calls and holds for every seed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/InexactGradientStronglyConvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: Errors may be biased and vary with the call index, query, and seed. No unbiasedness, independence, or mixing condition is imposed; the error bound holds pointwise for all seeds.

distinctive_assumptions.label: relative_error
distinctive_assumptions.details: Combined relative and absolute norm error, with 0≤α<1 and δ≥0. The accuracy regime requires 136δ²≤μ(1−α)²ε.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space, without a finite-dimensional restriction. E, L, x0, μ, and α are public; δ, R, and ε are hidden from the algorithm constructor, although the execution budget depends on them.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: Gradient.Public; LongTails/Setups/InexactGradientStronglyConvex.lean: Public, Params, and spec.publicInput; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar, with ε>0.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap requirement holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The standard smooth strongly convex objective is paired with a combined relative-plus-absolute oracle-error bound allowing arbitrary dependence, a noise-dependent accuracy regime, and hidden error, radius, and accuracy parameters.

descriptionHtml:
Inexact Gradient Strongly Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable, μ-strongly convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E, with quadratic upper curvature bound L≥μ>0. A given point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At x∈E, the oracle returns a vector g∈E with relative gradient error controlled by α∈[0,1) and additive error controlled by δ≥0. For a tolerance ε>0 compatible with this error, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the joint law of the algorithm’s and oracle’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The algorithm receives only E, L, x0, μ, and α; the parameters δ, R, and ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs. In addition to the ranges above, the parameters satisfy 136δ2≤μ(1−α)2ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and strong convexity). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For every x,y∈E, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2,f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+μ2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 2 (Inexact gradient oracle). Queries may be made at any point x∈E. Every oracle reply g∈E satisfies ∥g−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥+δ. This bound holds for every query history and every realization of the oracle randomness. Replies may depend on the history, and the oracle randomness may be dependent across calls. The algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle randomness.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈(8⋅Lμ⋅(1−α)+32⋅α2⋅Lμ⋅(1−α))⋅log⁡(1+2⋅L⋅R2ε)⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space, f is differentiable with global quadratic upper and lower models of curvature L and μ, where 0<μ≤L. A minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Every oracle reply obeys ∥g−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥+δ, with 0≤α<1 and δ,R≥0; errors may depend on the call and seed. The target is f(xN)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely, with ε>0 and 136δ2≤μ(1−α)2ε. The constructed method uses L,μ,α,x0; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

Inexact-gradient strongly convex optimization: InexactGradientStronglyConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AcceleratedInexactStronglyConvex (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+[κ1−α+α2κ1−α]ℓ)
(2) RE-AGM (Vasin and Gasnikov 2026, Thm. 6.1) O(1+(κ+ακ)ℓ); α≤1/3, ε≥Cmin{κ,α−1}δ2/μ. Euclidean space. (1): for κ−1/2≤α≤1/3, gain min{ακ,α−1}. At α=κ−1/4, O(1+κ1/2ℓ) instead of O(1+κ3/4ℓ). Certified floor drops to O(δ2/μ); extends to α<1.
(3) RE-AGM (Vasin et al. 2025, Thm. 4) O(1+κℓ); δ=0, α<c0κ−1/2. Euclidean space. (1): matches this rate; retains it up to α=O(κ−1/4) bounded away from 1, instead of O(κ−1/2). Scope: permits absolute error subject to its floor.
(4) RE-AGM (Vasin et al. 2025, Thm. 5) O(1+ακℓ); δ=0, κ−1/2/3≤α≤1/3. Euclidean space. (1): gain min{ακ,α−1} for κ−1/2≤α≤1/3; reaches κ1/4 at α=κ−1/4. Scope: adds absolute error subject to its floor.
(5) GD (Vasin and Gasnikov 2026, Thm. 5.2) O(1+κ(1+α)(1−α)3ℓ); ε≥C1+α(1−α)3δ2μ. Euclidean smooth PL functions; displayed initialization on the common strongly convex setup. (1): for large κ, α≤κ−1/4 and common admissible accuracy, O(1+κℓ) instead of O(1+κℓ). (1) requires strong convexity instead of the PL inequality.
(6) Fast gradient method (Gaucher et al. 2026, Thm. 3.3) O(1+κℓ); α=0, ε≥Cκδ2/μ. Euclidean space; additive-error specialization. (1): at α=0, certified floor δ2/μ instead of κδ2/μ in order; certifies acceleration below (6)’s threshold when δ2/μ≲ε≪κδ2/μ. Scope: adds relative error.

Abbr: κ=L/μ, ℓ=log⁡(1+LR2/ε); costs count inexact-gradient calls. C denotes a sufficiently large universal constant in sufficient accuracy conditions; α−1=+∞ at α=0. c0=(2−1)/(182). PL: ∥∇f(x)∥2≥2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆)).

import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.InexactGradientStronglyConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public extends toGradientPublic : LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.Public where
  μ : ℝ
  α : ℝ

structure Params extends Public where
  δ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.α ∧ p.α < 1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
    136 * p.δ ^ 2 ≤ p.μ * (1 - p.α) ^ 2 * p.ε
  admissible p f oracle :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, f y ≤ f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ + p.L / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ x y, f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ + p.μ / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 ≤ f y) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed - gradient f x‖ ≤ p.α * ‖gradient f x‖ + p.δ) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R)
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.InexactGradientStronglyConvex
